key_insight: The paper shows that vanilla on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) is just one special case of a broader policy-optimization framework with a tunable KL weight β. By exposing β as a controllable parameter, the method makes OPSD less brittle and easier to stabilize in practice.
problem_solved: It addresses the practical instability and heavy engineering burden of making on-policy self-distillation work reliably for reasoning language models.
method: Reformulate OPSD as policy optimization with a KL penalty to a reference model, where β controls the strength of anchoring.
Treat β as a tunable hyperparameter instead of fixing it implicitly at 1, allowing better control over exploration vs. stability.
Train with self-distillation while using the policy-optimization view to reduce brittleness and improve reliability.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a cleaner conceptual framework and a practical knob for stabilizing self-distillation-based training. It can reduce trial-and-error engineering and make reasoning-model improvement more reproducible.
visual_elements: A schematic showing OPSD as the β=1 point within a wider policy-optimization family
A slider or scale illustrating how changing β affects KL anchoring and model drift
A before/after diagram comparing brittle OPSD training vs. stabilized β-OPSD training
An icon-based flowchart: reference model → student update → self-distillation loop
paper_title: $β$-OPSD: Deriving with Policy Optimization, Training with Self-Distillation
paper_authors: Jiawei Xu, Minghui Liu, Juzheng Zhang, Tom Goldstein, Furong Huang
